fixture_name: Four-lane arterial improvement — US preliminary design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Queue storage/coordination between signals 650 ft apart on a high-accident corridor is a substantive, well-recognized safety issue appropriate to a preliminary design stage RSA.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal claim rests on a verbatim quoted fact (EV-US-001) recording the ~650 ft signal spacing, with the spillback inference explicitly labelled as derived rather than asserted as evidence.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety_concern under FHWA RSA semantics with no compliance claim conflated in, and road-user scoping stated transparently.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Recommendation is specific and actionable (signal coordination, Do Not Block Intersection signing, conspicuity enhancements) and viable at preliminary design, avoiding a null outcome.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists at both intersections are explicitly acknowledged, but VRU-specific impacts of the spillback mechanism (e.g., blocked crosswalks) are scoped out rather than analyzed, matching the 'not applicable but acknowledged' tier.
